1. The source for the plugin included in the JSON output is no longer the `yml` file with the docs, but the `py` file defining the filter itself. While this is also correct, it doesn't make the automatically generated "Edit on GitHub" link very helpful since in most cases you cannot edit the documentation there, but only the filter's/test's source code.
2. Aliases of tests are now listed as well. (That's nothing new, and to be expected, just wanted to to mention it here again for sake of completeness.)
3. ~~No filters and tests from collections are listed anymore.~~ Correction: they are listed, **but not when using `--metadata-dump`**, and thus they do not show up on the docsite anymore (assuming it is built with a newer version of antsibull-docs).

issue_context.title: ansible-doc fails to parse plugin docs
issue_context.body:
### Summary

When I try to run ansible-doc on the milestone branch (same result on devel) it fails when the token `DOCUMENTATION` is used anywhere else in the plugin. I believe https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/74963 introduced this bug. We initially saw this on the milestone branch sanity test failures for the kubernetes.core collection. https://github.com/ansible-collections/kubernetes.core/blob/95e2add65b4ade93a7ad770a8aa0386f90a9c831/plugins/connection/kubectl.py#L212 is what trips it up. As best I can tell, the new code looks for a `DOCUMENTATION` token anywhere and then uses the next string token as the doc string. In this case, it's `"{0}_command"` a few lines down.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

ansible-doc

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version
ansible [core 2.14.0.dev0] (milestone 2cc74b04c4) last updated 2022/05/05 08:26:56 (GMT -400)
  config file = None
  configured module search path = ['/home/mgraves/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /home/mgraves/git/ansible/lib/ansible
  ansible collection location = /home/mgraves/git:/home/mgraves/.ansible/collections
  executable location = /home/mgraves/git/ansible/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.8.8 (default, Mar  5 2021, 11:47:01) [GCC 10.2.1 20210110] (/home/mgraves/git/ansible/venv/bin/python)
  jinja version = 3.0.3
  libyaml = True
```


### Configuration

```console
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed
COLLECTIONS_PATHS(env: ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATH) = ['/home/mgraves/git', '/home/mgraves/.ansible/collections']
CONFIG_FILE() = None
```


### OS / Environment

Debian 11

### Steps to Reproduce

Using the latest release of kubernetes.core (2.3.1):
<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```yaml (paste below)
$ ansible-doc -t connection kubernetes.core.kubectl
ERROR! connection kubernetes.core.kubectl missing documentation (or could not parse documentation): did not find expected <document start>
  in "<unicode string>", line 1, column 4
```
You can also see similar failures for a really simple plugin like:
```yaml
DOCUMENTATION = r'''
    name: foo
    description:
      - foo module
'''

class Foo:
    DOCUMENTATION = None
    def __init__(self):
        foo = "bar"
```

### Expected Results

I expected the plugin documentation to be generated.

### Actual Results

```console
ERROR! connection kubernetes.core.kubectl missing documentation (or could not parse documentation): did not find expected <document start>
  in "<unicode string>", line 1, column 4
```

I see the commit that saying you'll fix this in a follow up, but it looks like an easy fix. On devel the deduping takes place in `_list_plugins_from_paths` after checking the plugin path is in the collection. Removing this and putting it there again fixes collection plugins shadowing core names.
```diff
diff --git a/lib/ansible/plugins/list.py b/lib/ansible/plugins/list.py
index 87f1c763ba..3fc43c7571 100644
--- a/lib/ansible/plugins/list.py
+++ b/lib/ansible/plugins/list.py
@@ -87,6 +87,7 @@ def _list_plugins_from_paths(ptype, dirs, collection, depth=0):
                                 if path not in ploader._extra_dirs:
                                     ploader.add_directory(path)
                                     added = True
+                                seen = set()
                                 for plugin in ploader.all():
                                     plugin_path = plugin._original_path
                                     if not is_subpath(plugin_path, path, real=True):
@@ -95,6 +96,10 @@ def _list_plugins_from_paths(ptype, dirs, collection, depth=0):
                                         continue
 
                                     plugin_name = get_composite_name(collection, plugin._load_name, path, depth)
+                                    if plugin_name in seen:
+                                        display.debug("%s skipped as duplicate" % plugin_name)
+                                        continue
+                                    seen.add(plugin_name)
                                     plugins[plugin_name] = plugin_path
                             finally:
                                 if added:
```
And doesn't seem to break anything in the test suite.
the problem is that 'all()' loading does it's own deduping
Yes, and this is in Jinja2Loader.all() so the 3 lines above would need to be removed in addition to the suggested diff.
then you allow dupes in the normal loading for templates?

normal loading for templates should be using fqcn though and it doesn't look like we dedupe regardless (on devel or with or without these lines). Maybe I'm misunderstanding, do you have a reproducer?

I tested with a collection that contains the same filter in two different filter files. The second loaded overwrites the first, no 'skipped as duplicate' debug msg in the output.

we do 'both', first we load 'all' to get builtin/legacy and then if fqcn is present we get the specific one (used to force reload of all with new extra dirs, but this PR changes it to use loader.get functions).
we 'could' make the dedupe=false parameter apply here and pass it in (it really only exists for base class to list the filter/test files since we dont dedupe on file name for those 2 plugins)

It seems like there is a pre-existing bug (on devel and this branch) with using ansible.legacy filters that shadow a builtin name. The builtin is always used. ansible.builtin doesn't need this because we know there aren't duplicates. Collections do have an issue with not deduping (last loaded wins), and this doesn't handle that (it does for `ansible-doc` but dedupes per unqualified plugin name so it's broken - either needs to happen in the caller `_list_plugins_from_paths` or the caller needs to pass more info for `Jinja2Loader.all()` like the collection path so it can check right).
i've been trying to avoid adding the colleciton to .all() .. the other option i was looking at was adding a `list` method to the plugin loader that allows passing a collection name/path
Can we load self.all() earlier, or just once instead?
i could cache them but would have to invalidate the cache on add_directory (i went back and forth on this)
the files that contain them are cached already via the 'module' import loading
